mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month indicates a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST drops > 10% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where INDPRO rises > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is negative, it signals a recessionary environment with low interest rates, which historically has led to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 1% and GDPC1 growth < 0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month for three consecutive months signals strong labor market conditions, which is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases > 200k for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 5% year-over-year and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it indicates strong consumer demand and a tight labor market, which historically has led to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: strong consumer demand and tight labor market
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where RSAFS YoY > 5% and UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases over three consecutive months.
